title: Etale sum extension and unbounded total tensor complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and let $u:U\to X$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $u_{\Sigma!}$ for sheafified sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] and $u^*=u^{-1}$ for exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Then $u_{\Sigma!}$ preserves all small direct sums. For arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes $P$ on $U$ and $H$ on $X$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], there is a canonical isomorphism of complexes, natural in both complexes,
$$\Psi_{P,H}:\operatorname{Tot}((u_{\Sigma!}P)\otimes_A H)\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{\Sigma!}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_A u^*H).$$
The functors $u_{\Sigma!}$ and $u^*$ on complexes here apply degreewise, and total tensor uses direct sums and differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_H$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. On the $(p,q)$ summand, before sum and tensor sheafification, the component of $\Psi$ sends $(s,m)\otimes h$ to $(s,m\otimes s^*h)$, where $s:W\to U$ is a lift over an etale test object $W\to X$, $m\in P^p(W,s)$, and $h\in H^q(W)$. It preserves the inclusion of each summand in total degree $p+q$ and the order of the tensor factors. The comparison is compatible with chain homotopies (degree $-1$ maps $h$ satisfying $f-g=dh+hd$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]) in both variables, hence gives a natural isomorphism on the homotopy categories (the same complexes, with chain maps taken modulo these homotopies). No boundedness, constructibility, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), canonical tensor-generator construction and sheaf projection isomorphism; agent expansion of its passage to unbounded total tensor complexes and the definition of K-flatness, rather than a verbatim assertion of this lemma.

proof.text:
Put $L=u_{\Sigma!}$ and $R=u^*$. The map $u$ is etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] gives $L\dashv R$ for exactly the lift-indexed sum extension in the statement and constant-$A$ module sheaves. For any small family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to its discrete indexing category. The module-sheaf categories have all direct sums, as specified in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Thus the canonical map
$$c_{(M_i)}:\bigoplus_i LM_i\xrightarrow{\sim}L(\bigoplus_i M_i)$$
is an isomorphism, characterized by $c\iota_i=L\iota_i$. This proves direct-sum preservation, including the empty sum. For a family of maps $a_i:M_i\to N_i$, the equality $L(\bigoplus_i a_i)c_M=c_N(\bigoplus_i La_i)$ follows after precomposing with each $\iota_i$, since both sides then equal $L(\iota_i a_i)$. This fixes the naturality of the particular comparison used below.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1), applied to the etale sum adjunction

proof.text: Use the existing additive instances for L and R. In particular AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.additive_upperStar is proved from the upperStar/lowerStar adjunction, and the lower-shriek functor is additive by its binary-product preservation. No comparison with the alternative SheafOfModules encoding is used. Applying the additive functors degreewise preserves square-zero and chain-map equations, giving the complexes LP and RH of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] for the sum-extension functor [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension].

source.place: Section 010V, cochain complexes and additive functors; lift-indexed formula from the cited definition

proof.text:
Apply the proved upstream canonical isomorphism AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.etaleLowerShriekTensorIso (in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.LowerShriek.EtaleMapProjection) and its hom_naturality lemma with $e=u$, $M=P^p$, $N=H^q$. Its hypotheses hold because $u$ is separated etale of finite type and $A$ is commutative. Write its natural sheaf isomorphism as
$$a_{p,q}:LP^p\otimes_A H^q\xrightarrow{\sim}L(P^p\otimes_A RH^q).$$
For $I_n=\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$, define
$$\Psi^n=c_{(P^p\otimes_A RH^q)_{I_n}}\circ\bigoplus_{I_n}a_{p,q}.$$
By Step 1 and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] this is an isomorphism from the degree-$n$ term of the left total tensor to the degree-$n$ term of the right side. Its inverse is $(\bigoplus a_{p,q}^{-1})c^{-1}$. Moreover $\Psi^n\iota_{p,q}=L\iota_{p,q}\,a_{p,q}$, so it preserves the specified summand inclusions. On the presheaf generators its formula is exactly $(s,m)\otimes h\mapsto(s,m\otimes s^*h)$ from the cited projection lemma; no tensor factor is permuted. The Lean statement already defines the component as the inverse of this specific upstream isomorphism, so the stronger separate existence theorem with section and geometric-stalk clauses is not required.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), generator formula; homology.tex Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex), direct-sum terms

proof.text:
Naturality of the proved upstream canonical isomorphism AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.etaleLowerShriekTensorIso (in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.LowerShriek.EtaleMapProjection) and its hom_naturality lemma, applied separately to the two differentials, gives
$$a_{p+1,q}(Ld_P^p\otimes1)=L(d_P^p\otimes1)a_{p,q},\qquad
 a_{p,q+1}(1\otimes d_H^q)=L(1\otimes Rd_H^q)a_{p,q}.$$
The second differential has coefficient $(-1)^p$ on both sides, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. By additivity from Step 2, $L$ respects this coefficient and the sum of the two differentials. Precompose the desired equality $d\Psi^n=\Psi^{n+1}d$ with $\iota_{p,q}$; the displayed equations and $c\iota=L\iota$ from Step 1 make its two components equal in bidegrees $(p+1,q)$ and $(p,q+1)$. Since a map from a coproduct is determined by its restrictions to the summands, the equality holds. Thus the $\Psi^n$ form a chain map. Their degreewise inverses also form a chain map: multiply this equality on the left and right by the appropriate inverses. They give the claimed isomorphism of complexes, with the stated sign convention.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex), differential; naturality of the generator construction in more-etale.tex Tag 0GKF

proof.text:
For chain maps $f:P\to P'$ and $g:H\to H'$, the same sheaf naturality gives
$$a'_{p,q}(Lf^p\otimes g^q)=L(f^p\otimes Rg^q)a_{p,q}.$$
Using the naturality of $c$ proved in Step 1 and taking the direct sum in each degree yields
$$\Psi_{P',H'}\operatorname{Tot}(Lf\otimes g)=L\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes Rg)\Psi_{P,H}.$$
Here the tensor maps are precisely those of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the $a_{p,q}$ are those of the proved upstream canonical isomorphism AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.etaleLowerShriekTensorIso (in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.LowerShriek.EtaleMapProjection) and its hom_naturality lemma. This proves naturality in both variables, with identities and compositions inherited from the component formulas.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), naturality; agent assembly on the total summands

proof.text:
Let $h^p:P^p\to P'^{p-1}$ satisfy $f-g=d_{P'}h+hd_P$, the homotopy equation of [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For total tensor with fixed $H$, define a degree-$-1$ map on the $(p,q)$ summand by $Lh^p\otimes1$ on the left, and by $L(h^p\otimes1)$ on the right (with the sum comparisons of Step 1). Using the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the $H$-differential terms in $dS+Sd$ have coefficients $(-1)^{p-1}$ and $(-1)^p$ and cancel. The remaining terms are $L(d_{P'}h+hd_P)\otimes1=L(f-g)\otimes1$ on the left, and $L((d_{P'}h+hd_P)\otimes1)=L((f-g)\otimes1)$ on the right. Thus these are the induced homotopies. Naturality of the proved upstream canonical isomorphism AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.etaleLowerShriekTensorIso (in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.LowerShriek.EtaleMapProjection) and its hom_naturality lemma for the sheaf morphism $h^p$ gives
$$a_{p-1,q}(Lh^p\otimes1)=L(h^p\otimes1)a_{p,q}.$$
After inclusion into total degree $p+q-1$ and summation, this says exactly that $\Psi$ intertwines these degree-$-1$ maps, not merely their boundaries.

source.place: Section 010V, displayed cochain homotopy equation; Tag 012Z, signed total differential; agent calculation

proof.text:
For a homotopy $k^q:H^q\to H'^{q-1}$ with $f-g=d_{H'}k+kd_H$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], take on the $(p,q)$ summand the degree-$-1$ maps $(-1)^p1\otimes k^q$ on the left and $L((-1)^p1\otimes Rk^q)$ on the right. In $dS+Sd$ the $P$-differential terms have coefficients $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$ and cancel. Each of the remaining two terms has coefficient $(-1)^{2p}=1$, so their sum is $1\otimes(d_{H'}k+kd_H)=1\otimes(f-g)$, or its image under $R$ and $L$, as appropriate. This is the differential convention of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The equality
$$a_{p,q-1}(1\otimes k^q)=L(1\otimes Rk^q)a_{p,q}$$
is sheaf naturality in the proved upstream canonical isomorphism AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.etaleLowerShriekTensorIso (in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.LowerShriek.EtaleMapProjection) and its hom_naturality lemma. Multiplying by $(-1)^p$ and using the sum comparisons proves compatibility of $\Psi$ with these homotopies as well. The component maps and the homotopies have one target summand for each source summand, and the differential has two, so every construction is defined by coproduct maps for arbitrary unbounded complexes. Steps 6 and 7 show that both bifunctors respect homotopy classes in either variable. Quotienting the naturality equality of Step 5 therefore gives a natural isomorphism on the homotopy categories; the inverse descends since it is already an inverse chain map. No flatness, constructibility, or boundedness was used.
